title: Sleepy Princess in the Demon Castle
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Princess Syalis has been kidnapped by the Demon King and held in his castle while a hero sets out to rescue her. Bored and unable to sleep well, she ignores the danger and devotes herself to getting comfortable, raiding the castle for bedding, such as fur from her teddy-bear demon guards and a magical shield turned air mattress. Her schemes often end in her own accidental death or the deaths of minor demons, undone by the castle's demon cleric, and she comes to treat the castle as home while her clumsy hero-fiance fails to arrive (Wikipedia; VIZ blurbs; AniList Slapstick, Episodic).
life_message: Rest and comfort are worth pursuing, and even 'enemies' can become a kind of household.

content.note: Killing ghost-shroud demons for cloth is a running joke; Syalis's own accidental deaths, all reversed by the cleric (Wikipedia; VIZ blurb; MU Ruthless Female Lead, Scissors).
Demons and monsters are cute and harmless in tone.
Succubus and Yuri tags at low rank (AniList); nothing explicit noted (to verify).
Syalis repeatedly dies through reckless sleep schemes, played as comedy (VIZ blurb).
Using scissors on living creatures and reading a 'Forbidden Grimoire' as bedtime reading, as jokes (VIZ blurb; MU Scissors).

dominant: Comfort-seeking comedy; absurdism; captor-captive role reversal

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Syalis ignores her captors' threats; no honor feuds.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The captive does what she pleases inside the castle.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Demon staff become a makeshift household (AniList Ensemble Cast).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Princess and Demon King roles reversed; hierarchy mocked.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Fairy-tale conventions parodied rather than honored.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Quality of life (sleep) over survival is the joke.

folkways.japan: The comedy plays on video-game and fairy-tale conventions of hero, demon king and captive princess familiar in Japanese pop culture.

delivery.evidence: Episodic gag comedy with no stated message per Wikipedia and VIZ blurbs (to verify).
delivery.note: Demons who want order are comic victims, yet they are drawn affectionately.

winners_losers: Syalis always gets her rest; the demons who try to keep order lose. Sympathy is with comfort over duty.
